title: ArboReaders Book Club
summary: CHA, in collaboration with the Nature of Reading Bookshop in Madison, is excited to share our next ArboReaders book choice, Fearless, Sleepless, Deathless: What Fungi Taught Me about Nourishment, Poison, Ecology, Hidden Histories, Zombies, and Black Survival by Maria Pinto. Read at your leisure and the join the discussion at our next meeting. Interested individuals are welcome to join us, whether you have attended in the past or not. This is a free event for adults 18 years and older. Naturalist, forager, and educator Maria Pinto offers a stunning debut book that uncovers strange and beautiful fungal connections between the natural and human worlds. She mingles reportage, research, memoir, and nature writing, touching on topics that range from Black farmers’ domestication of the unforgettable aroma of truffles to the possibility that enslaved people wielded mycological poisons against their enslavers. Pinto brings a new perspective and a distinctive literary voice to this mix of environmental and lived history, and every page sings with her enthusiasm for the networks in which we are embedded: fungal, ecological, ancestral, and communal. Join her in pursuit of beautiful, perplexing, delicious, and deadly mushrooms as she explores this understudied kingdom’s awe-inspiring diversity and discovers how fungi have been used by people, especially those on the margins, for survival, pleasure, revelation, and revolution.

title: Light of Knowledge: A Diwali Celebration
venue: North Edison Temporary Branch · Meeting Room 1
summary: Celebrate the festival of lights with Kalagangothri in a captivating afternoon of Indian classical dance and music inspired by the spirit of Diwali! This enriching program honors India's rich artistic traditions, spiritual wisdom, and cultural heritage, sharing the message of light, knowledge, and harmony across generation through the beauty of Indian classical dance, Carnatic vocal music, and violin. Program Highlights: Deepanjali - An Offering of Light: A graceful dance celebrating the lamp as a symbol of hope, wisdom, and the triumph of light over darkness. Swaranjali - An Offering of Music: A musical tribute to the beauty and devotion of India's classical arts. Namo Namo Bharathambe - Salutations to Mother India: A dance honoring India's heritage, spiritual traditions, and enduring cultural values. Layanadha - A Carnatic Musical Concert: A 40-minute performance featuring Carnatic vocal music and violin. Thillana - A Joyous Finale: An energetic Bharatanatyam performance celebrating rhythm, movement, and the joy of classical dance. About the Kalagangothri Foundation: Guru Smt. Akhilandeshwari Vasudevamurthy is an award-winning Bharatanatyam dancer, educator, and co-founder of Kalagangothri Foundation, based. With more than 35 years of experience, she is dedicated to preserving and sharing Indian classical arts through performance, teaching, and cultural education. A recipient of the prestigious Purandaranugraha Prashasthi Award and two New Jersey State Council on the Arts Master Grants, she has trained hundreds of students and pioneered the integration of Bharatanatyam into public school curricula. title: John Lennon: Life, Legend, and Legacy
summary: A presentation by John Paul Groom About the program The beginning of The Beatles took place at a summer garden fete at St. Peter's Church in Woolton, Liverpool, marking a watershed point in music history. When John Lennon was 16 years old and performing with his skiffle band The Quarrymen, a common acquaintance called Ivan Vaughan, introduced him to Paul McCartney, who was 15 years old at the time. This one-of-a-kind partnership altered the course of music irrevocably, and our presenter will trace its history. About the presenter John Paul Groom gives historical presentations about the 1960s, with a particular focus on The Beatles. Originally from Liverpool, Groom resided in the same city as John Lennon and George Harrison, participated in the same Sunday school as John Lennon, and went to the same high school as Paul McCartney and George Harrison.

title: The Hip Hop Nutcracker
summary: A holiday mash-up for the whole family, The Hip Hop Nutcracker returns for another spectacular tour. Directed and choreographed by Tony and Olivier® Award-nominated Jennifer Weber, this contemporary dance spectacle is a re-mixed and re-imagined version of the classic, smashing hip hop dance and Tchaikovsky’s timeless music together into a heart-stirring and inspirational holiday event. The Hip Hop Nutcracker is brought to life by a powerhouse cast of a dozen all-star dancers, a DJ, a violinist, and an MC. Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season. Innovative digital graffiti and visuals transform the landscape of E. T. A. Hoffmann’s beloved story from traditional 19th Century Germany to the vibrant, diverse sights and sounds of contemporary New York City. Grab your family and friends and let the dynamic performers of The Hip Hop Nutcracker take you on a journey that celebrates love, community and the magic of the holiday season.

title: LGBTQ+ Book Discussion: These Heathens, by Mia McKenzie
registration: Register if required on official event page
summary: The Newark Public Library LGBTQ+ Resource Center presents a monthly book discussion group, where all backgrounds and identities are welcome and encouraged to participate. Join us at the Main Library, LGBTQ+ Resource Center, for a group discussion of These Heathens, by Mia McKenzie From the “razor-sharp and outrageously funny” (Taylor Jenkins Reid) mind of Mia McKenzie comes a vibrant novel exploring how one weekend can change your whole life. FINALIST FOR THE LOS ANGELES TIMES BOOK PRIZE • LONGLISTED FOR THE ANDREW CARNEGIE MEDAL AND THE ASPEN WORDS LITERARY PRIZE • A CHICAGO PUBLIC LIBRARY BEST BOOK OF THE YEAR Dear Lord, please forgive me for the sins I’ve committed. And for the one I’m still planning to commit tomorrow. Amen. Where do you get an abortion in 1960 Georgia, especially if your small town’s midwife goes to the same church as your parents? For 17-year-old Doris Steele, the answer is Atlanta, where her favorite teacher, Mrs. Lucas, calls upon her brash, wealthy childhood best friend, Sylvia, for help. While waiting to hear from the doctor who has agreed to do the procedure, Doris spends the weekend scandalized by, but drawn to, the people who move in and out of Sylvia’s orbit: celebrities whom Doris has seen in the pages of Jet and Ebony, civil rights leaders such as Coretta Scott King and Diane Nash, women who dance close together, boys who flirt too hard and talk too much, atheists! And even more shocking? Mrs. Lucas seems right at home. From the guests at a queer kickback to the student activists at a SNCC conference, Doris suddenly finds herself surrounded by so many people who seem to know exactly who or what they want. Doris knows she doesn’t want a baby, but what does she want? Will this trip help her find out? These Heathens is a funny, poignant story about Black women’s obligations and ambitions, what we owe to ourselves, and the transformative power of leaving your bubble, even for just one chaotic weekend. Free copies of the book are available and will be provided upon request*. *Please note that free copies of the book are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis, and will only be distributed to those who commit to attending the discussion.

title: [Zoom] Successfully Navigating College Admissions This Fall
summary: By Stand Out for College (www. standoutforcollege. com) A repeat of the presentation by the same name The session will cover current college admissions trends and strategies, the evolving test optional environment, the importance of researching and visiting colleges to find the right fit, and key timelines and action steps that can make this fall productive while easing stress around the college admissions process. The workshop will also take a close look at the holistic admissions review process, including what admissions officers value when evaluating applicants and how students can develop a strong personal narrative that reflects their strengths, interests, character, and experiences. Another focus will be on the role of community service and the growing importance of meaningful "passion projects. " Presenters will discuss how students can turn their interests, values, and experiences into authentic activities that foster personal growth, demonstrate character, and show positive impact. Admissions officers place great emphasis on character, and thoughtful service can help students show initiative, empathy, and a genuine commitment to helping their communities. This program is recommended for parents and their high school teens. It provides a clear and strategic overview of what students should prioritize this fall for a successful college admissions journey and how to approach the process with confidence and less stress. The presentation will be led by Ron Feuchs and Jackie Tepper, partners at Stand Out For College, LLC (www. com).

title: Diwali Evening Concert
venue: Sri Venketeswara Temple and Community Center
venueName: Sri Venketeswara Temple and Community Center
summary: This Diwali, join us for an extraordinary musical tribute celebrating the timeless legacy of the legendary maestro, Late Pandit Jitendra Abhisheki. Revered as one of India’s most influential composers, vocalists, and visionaries, Pandit Abhisheki transformed Hindustani classical music and Marathi musical theatre through his unparalleled artistry and innovation. Presented as a heartfelt retrospective of his most beloved musical works, this special concert brings together three distinguished torchbearers of his rich artistic tradition: acclaimed vocalist Shounak Abhisheki, rising artist Abhed Abhisheki, and one of his foremost disciples, Makarand Hingne. Through unforgettable compositions, devotional masterpieces, natya sangeet, and classical treasures, the evening offers a rare opportunity to experience the depth, beauty, and enduring influence of Pandit Abhisheki’s musical genius. As families gather to celebrate the Festival of Lights, this concert promises an inspiring morning of reflection, nostalgia, and artistic brilliance. Join us in honoring a legacy that continues to illuminate generations of music lovers around the world. Evening Concert • Approx. 160 minutes including intermission. Hot snacks & beverages available for purchase prior to doors opening

title: The Irish Tenors: A Family Christmas
summary: Celebrate the magic of the season with The Irish Tenors: A Family Christmas. A cherished holiday tradition, this heartwarming concert features beloved Christmas classics alongside timeless Irish favorites, performed with the soaring harmonies that have made The Irish Tenors one of the world’s most beloved vocal trios. Their acclaimed PBS specials and best-selling recordings have introduced millions to a sound that has become synonymous with the holidays. Featuring Anthony Kearns, celebrated for his rich lyric tenor and acclaimed performances at the White House and Carnegie Hall; Ronan Tynan, the internationally renowned tenor and Paralympic gold medalist whose powerful voice has captivated audiences for decades; and Patrick Hyland, an acclaimed Irish tenor known for his expressive performances and exceptional vocal artistry, the trio brings warmth, joy, and elegance to every performance. Blending treasured holiday favorites from their best-selling Christmas album We Three Kings with beloved Irish songs, The Irish Tenors: A Family Christmas is a festive celebration filled with beautiful melodies, heartfelt storytelling, and the spirit of the season. It’s a holiday tradition the whole family will treasure.

title: Meet & Make
registration: Register if required on official event page
summary: Formerly known as Meet & Mend, Meet & Make is our monthly hand-sewing class. Jump into a guided hand-sewing project, learn new skills, and be in community. Now with a new instructor, Mark Menzie, who brings hands-on guidance, real industry experience, and a welcoming approach to learning how to sew and mend with confidence. ABOUT MARK MENZIE Mark E. Menzie is a Newark-based fashion designer, stylist, and educator with over a decade of experience in the fashion industry. He is the founder and creative director of Menzie by Design, a youth-focused fashion and lifestyle brand centered on creativity, craftsmanship, and self-expression. A graduate of the Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT), Mark has studied fashion design, trend forecasting in France and Italy, and fashion business and entrepreneurship. His professional background spans luxury retail, styling, product development, and community-based arts education. As an instructor, Mark is passionate about making fashion accessible and culturally relevant for young people. His classes blend traditional sewing skills with hands-on crafts, storytelling, and design history—often drawing inspiration from childhood techniques like paper dolls, patchwork, and upcycling. Through his teaching, he empowers students to build confidence, creativity, and practical skills while seeing themselves reflected in the world of fashion and design. ABOUT MADE@NPL Made@NPL is a community resource. Made@NPL supports creative entrepreneurs with business reference services and programming related to creativity, entrepreneurship, and making things. Made@NPL was funded by a generous grant from the PNC Foundation.

title: 23 A Memoir with Author Moe Lajterman
venue: Shimon and Sara Birnbaum Jewish Community Center
venueName: Shimon and Sara Birnbaum Jewish Community Center
summary: One moment can change a family forever. Join us for a moving evening with author Moe Lajterman as he discusses 23: A Memoir, a deeply personal story of family, immigration, loss, and the memories that connect one generation to the next. Lajterman traces his family’s journey from Buenos Aires, Argentina, to building a new life. At the heart of the memoir is his older brother, Marcelo Lajterman, whose life was cut short in the 1970 Marshall University football team plane crash—a tragedy that forever changed his family. Through stories of love, resilience, grief, and remembrance, 23 explores not only what a family loses in tragedy, but what remains and is carried forward. The evening will be moderated by Josh Leibner and will include a conversation with Moe Lajterman about the experiences and memories behind the book. FEE: $10/JCC Members; $15/Community Member

title: A VERY BARRY CHRISTMAS: Daybreak Manilow Tribute Holiday Edition!
summary: One of the most authentic tribute acts ever to hit the music scene, DAYBREAK “The Music & Passion of Barry Manilow” takes audiences on a musical journey back to the ‘70s with some holiday classics sprinkled! DAYBREAK “The Music & Passion of Barry Manilow” will have fans experiencing Barry Manilow’s greatest hits the way they remember them. Barry Manilow is considered by many to be one of the most successful pop artists ever and became an international star with a string of hits combining heart on the sleeve sentiment, with lyrical pop craftsmanship and a slick, highly orchestrated production. Barry Manilow recorded and released 51 Top 40 singles including 13 that reached No. 1. Led by veteran musician and accomplished pianist Joe Hite, DAYBREAK brings to life timeless classics like “Mandy,” “Can’t Smile Without You” and the foot-stomping rhythm of “Copacabana” just to name a few. The Very Barry Christmas edition includes some festive holiday classics sprinkled.

title: Sponsor & Decorate a Tree for our Holiday Open House!
summary: (children & adults) Calling local businesses, organizations, families, schools, and scout groups! Sponsor a tree, bring your creativity, and help us fill Reeves-Reed Arboretum with holiday cheer! Decorated trees will be featured at our Holiday Open House, where visitors can vote for their favorites., we will be holding our annual Holiday Open House, and we invite YOU to help make it a success! STEP 1: Sign up to sponsor and decorate a tree! RRA will provide and set up the trees, you just need the decorations. We will have a limited number of trees, so don’t wait to sign up. STEP 2: Decorate! Gather your family, friends, or colleagues and come to the Arboretum, to create your display. Be creative, there will be prizes! STEP 3: Return with your two complimentary tickets for the Holiday Open House to enjoy the fun! Sip ‘n Shop at our Holiday Market for unique gifts, holiday décor, delicious treats, and more! Explore the Winter Story Walk, Candy Cane Lane, and make a Winter Craft. Enjoy Live Holiday Carolers and of course touring the trees and voting for your favorite one! STEP 4: After the event, you are welcome to take your tree home or remove the decorations and leave it on the Arboretum grounds. We can use the trees to make mulch or use the branches to protect our beds from frost during the winter months. Details. Answers to frequently asked questions: Trees are approximately 5-6 feet tall and are in stands. If you choose to string lights, please make sure they are battery operated since electricity is not available on the grounds. It is recommended that ornaments be able to withstand rain/snow and are secure in case of windy conditions. Balloons and candles are not permitted. Additional items/props can be placed under or near your tree. Get creative! Some previous themes have included: Wordle, Goats, Sports, Cooking, etc. Each tree will have an assigned number, the title of your tree, and the name of your group/business. You will receive further details about the decorating sessions via email a few days before. First and second place prizes will be awarded. Winners will be notified within a day or two of the event, and we will post the winning trees on social media. If you are taking your tree home after the event on Sunday, it can be removed from the stand and taken If you are coming back for the tree, please remove it by Wednesday. If you are not keeping the tree, all decorations, props, etc. SPONSOR PRICING: Nonprofits/Families/School and Scout Groups $125; Corporate/Businesses $150 IMPORTANT: Please indicate in the details box on the check-out page that this donation is for Sponsoring a Festival Tree. Please also indicate the name of your group/family/business/organization. Need additional tickets for the event? Thank you for supporting our non-profit public gardens, grounds, and environmental education programs! HAVE ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS? Please contact Jackie Kondel at j. kondel@reeves-reedarboretum. org.

Jo is trying to sell her stories for publication, but the publishers are not interested – her friend, Professor Bhaer, tells her that she has to do better and write more from herself. Begrudgingly taking this advice, Jo weaves the story of herself and her sisters and their experience growing up.

title: SONS OF SERENDIP: Christmas Beyond the Lights
summary: BACK BY POPULAR DEMAND FOR THE THIRD YEAR IN A ROW! Billboard charting classical-crossover quartet, Sons of Serendip, won the hearts of fans and judges alike as finalists on America’s Got Talent (NBC) with their ethereal and emotionally stirring interpretations of pop music, arranged with a unique blend of vocals, harp, piano, and cello.
